```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)

data <- read.csv("aims-sml-2024-2025-data.csv")

head(data)
str(data)

n <- nrow(data)

  geom_point(color = "blue", alpha = 0.6) +

       x = "x",
       y = "y") +

# Inspect the target variable

# Analysis: If `y` is continuous, it’s a regression task. If `y` is categorical (e.g., factors), it’s a classification task.

# Check the data type of y
if (is.numeric(data$y)) {
  cat("This is a regression task because the target variable y is numeric and continuous.\n")
} else if (is.factor(data$y) || is.character(data$y)) {
  cat("This is a classification task because the target variable y is categorical.\n")
} else {
  cat("The nature of the task cannot be determined from the data type of y.\n")
}
# The dataset consists of two columns, x and y, both of which are numeric and continuous (float64). Since the target variable y is continuous, this is a regression task.

#Justification:
#The target variable y represents continuous values (e.g., real numbers).
#Regression tasks involve predicting continuous outputs, which aligns with the data type of y.
```

#PART 3
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(caret)
library(lattice)
# Read in the dataset
data <- read.csv("aims-sml-2024-2025-data.csv")

# Fit a simple linear regression model (for OLS estimator)

anova_model <- lm(y ~ poly(x, optimal_degree, raw = TRUE), data = data)


# View the model summary
summary(anova_model)


# Function to perform k-fold cross-validation for polynomial regression
cv_poly <- function(data, p, k = 5) {
  # Set up polynomial formula based on degree p
  formula <- as.formula(paste("y ~ poly(x, ", p, ", raw = TRUE)", sep = ""))
  
  # Set up cross-validation method
  train_control <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = k)
  
  # Train the model using polynomial regression
  model <- train(formula, data = data, method = "lm", trControl = train_control)
  
  # Return the mean cross-validation error
  return(mean(model$resample$RMSE)) # RMSE is a good metric for regression
}

# Try different polynomial degrees
degrees <- 1:10
cv_errors <- sapply(degrees, function(p) cv_poly(data, p))

# Identify the optimal polynomial degree (the one with the minimum cross-validation error)
optimal_degree <- degrees[which.min(cv_errors)]
cat("The optimal polynomial degree is:", optimal_degree, "\n")

# Plot the cross-validation error
plot(degrees, cv_errors, type = "b", col = "blue", pch = 19, 
     xlab = "Degree of Polynomial (p)", ylab = "Cross-Validation Error", 
     main = "Cross-Validation Error vs Polynomial Degree")

# Highlight the optimal degree on the plot
points(optimal_degree, min(cv_errors), col = "red", pch = 19)
text(optimal_degree, min(cv_errors), labels = paste("Optimal degree:", optimal_degree), pos = 4, col = "red")

# Function to compute training error (empirical risk) for polynomial regression
train_error <- function(data, p) {
  # Set up polynomial formula based on degree p
  formula <- as.formula(paste("y ~ poly(x, ", p, ", raw = TRUE)", sep = ""))
  
  # Fit the model
  model <- lm(formula, data = data)
  
  # Predict on training data
  predictions <- predict(model, data)
  
  # Calculate training error (RMSE)
  error <- sqrt(mean((data$y - predictions)^2))
  return(error)
}

# Compute training errors for different polynomial degrees
train_errors <- sapply(degrees, function(p) train_error(data, p))

# Plot both cross-validation and training errors
plot(degrees, cv_errors, type = "b", col = "blue", pch = 19, 
     xlab = "Degree of Polynomial (p)", ylab = "Error", 
     main = "Cross-Validation and Training Error vs Polynomial Degree")
lines(degrees, train_errors, type = "b", col = "red", pch = 19)
# Step 6: Fit and Plot the Final Model
final_model <- lm(y ~ poly(x, optimal_degree, raw = TRUE), data = data)
summary(final_model)

ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ poly(x, optimal_degree, raw = TRUE), color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = paste("Polynomial Regression (Degree =", optimal_degree, ")"),
    x = "x", y = "y"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()





```
#PART 4
```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(caret)

# Load data
data <- read.csv("aims-sml-2024-2025-data.csv")
data$x <- as.numeric(data$x)
data$y <- as.numeric(data$y)

# Simplest Model (Degree 1)
simplest_model <- lm(y ~ poly(x, 1, raw = TRUE), data = data)

# Optimal Model (Degree determined by CV)
cv_poly_rmse <- function(data, degree, k = 5) {
    formula <- as.formula(paste("y ~ poly(x, ", degree, ", raw = TRUE)", sep = ""))
    train_control <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = k)
    model <- train(formula, data = data, method = "lm", trControl = train_control)
    return(mean(model$resample$RMSE))  # Return mean RMSE
}
degrees <- 1:10
cv_errors <- sapply(degrees, function(d) cv_poly_rmse(data, d))
optimal_degree <- degrees[which.min(cv_errors)]
optimal_model <- lm(y ~ poly(x, optimal_degree, raw = TRUE), data = data)

# Overly Complex Model (Degree 10)
overly_complex_model <- lm(y ~ poly(x, 10, raw = TRUE), data = data)

# Plot all models
ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_point(color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
    stat_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ poly(x, 1, raw = TRUE), color = "blue", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1, aes(linetype = "Simplest Model")) +
    stat_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ poly(x, optimal_degree, raw = TRUE), color = "green", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1, aes(linetype = "Optimal Model")) +
    stat_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ poly(x, 10, raw = TRUE), color = "red", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1, aes(linetype = "Overly Complex Model")) +
    ggtitle("Models Comparison: Simplest, Optimal, and Overly Complex") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(linetype = "Model") +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Simplest Model" = "solid", "Optimal Model" = "dashed", "Overly Complex Model" = "dotdash")) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
# Stochastic Hold-Out Validation
set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility
S <- 100
simplest_errors <- numeric(S)
optimal_errors <- numeric(S)
complex_errors <- numeric(S)

for (i in 1:S) {
    # Random split
    train_indices <- sample(1:nrow(data), size = 0.7 * nrow(data))
    train_data <- data[train_indices, ]
    test_data <- data[-train_indices, ]
    
    # Simplest Model
    simplest_model <- lm(y ~ poly(x, 1, raw = TRUE), data = train_data)
    simplest_pred <- predict(simplest_model, test_data)
    simplest_errors[i] <- sqrt(mean((test_data$y - simplest_pred)^2))
    
    # Optimal Model
    optimal_model <- lm(y ~ poly(x, optimal_degree, raw = TRUE), data = train_data)
    optimal_pred <- predict(optimal_model, test_data)
    optimal_errors[i] <- sqrt(mean((test_data$y - optimal_pred)^2))
    
    # Overly Complex Model
    overly_complex_model <- lm(y ~ poly(x, 10, raw = TRUE), data = train_data)
    complex_pred <- predict(overly_complex_model, test_data)
    complex_errors[i] <- sqrt(mean((test_data$y - complex_pred)^2))
}

# Boxplot of Test Errors
error_data <- data.frame(
    Model = rep(c("Simplest", "Optimal", "Overly Complex"), each = S),
    Error = c(simplest_errors, optimal_errors, complex_errors)
)

ggplot(error_data, aes(x = Model, y = Error, fill = Model)) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    ggtitle("Test Errors Across Models (100 Splits)") +
    theme_minimal()
# Calculate and Print Bias for Each Model
calculate_bias <- function(predicted, actual) {
    return(mean(predicted - actual))
}

# Bias Calculation Using Hold-Out Validation
simplest_biases <- numeric(S)
optimal_biases <- numeric(S)
complex_biases <- numeric(S)

for (i in 1:S) {
    # Random split
    train_indices <- sample(1:nrow(data), size = 0.7 * nrow(data))
    train_data <- data[train_indices, ]
    test_data <- data[-train_indices, ]
    
    # Simplest Model
    simplest_model <- lm(y ~ poly(x, 1, raw = TRUE), data = train_data)
    simplest_pred <- predict(simplest_model, test_data)
    simplest_biases[i] <- calculate_bias(simplest_pred, test_data$y)
    
    # Optimal Model
    optimal_model <- lm(y ~ poly(x, optimal_degree, raw = TRUE), data = train_data)
    optimal_pred <- predict(optimal_model, test_data)
    optimal_biases[i] <- calculate_bias(optimal_pred, test_data$y)
    
    # Overly Complex Model
    overly_complex_model <- lm(y ~ poly(x, 10, raw = TRUE), data = train_data)
    complex_pred <- predict(overly_complex_model, test_data)
    complex_biases[i] <- calculate_bias(complex_pred, test_data$y)
}

# Print Mean Bias Values
cat("Mean Bias for Simplest Model:", mean(simplest_biases), "\n")
cat("Mean Bias for Optimal Model:", mean(optimal_biases), "\n")
cat("Mean Bias for Overly Complex Model:", mean(complex_biases), "\n")

```

```{r}
colnames(data)
colnames(data) <- c("x", "y")
# Fit the optimal model
optimal_formula <- as.formula(paste("y ~ poly(x, ", optimal_degree, ", raw = TRUE)", sep = ""))
optimal_model <- lm(optimal_formula, data = data)

# Perform ANOVA
anova_results <- anova(optimal_model)
print(anova_results)
summary(anova_results)
# Generate data for predictions
new_data <- data.frame(x = seq(min(data$x), max(data$x), length.out = 100))

# Compute confidence intervals
confidence <- predict(optimal_model, newdata = new_data, interval = "confidence")

# Compute prediction intervals
prediction <- predict(optimal_model, newdata = new_data, interval = "prediction")

# Plot the data, regression line, and bands
plot(data$x, data$y, col = "blue", pch = 19, main = "Confidence and Prediction Bands")
lines(new_data$x, confidence[, "fit"], col = "red", lwd = 2)  # Regression line
lines(new_data$x, confidence[, "lwr"], col = "blue", lty = 2)  # Confidence lower
lines(new_data$x, confidence[, "upr"], col = "blue", lty = 2)  # Confidence upper
lines(new_data$x, prediction[, "lwr"], col = "green", lty = 2)  # Prediction lower
lines(new_data$x, prediction[, "upr"], col = "green", lty = 2)  # Prediction upper
legend("topright", legend = c("Regression Line", "Confidence Band", "Prediction Band"),
       col = c("red", "blue", "green"), lty = c(1, 2, 2))

# Interpretation
cat("Interpretation of Confidence and Prediction Bands:\n")
cat("1. Confidence Bands show where the true regression line is expected to lie with 95% confidence.\n")
cat("2. Prediction Bands show where future observations are likely to fall with 95% confidence.\n")
cat("3. Wider bands indicate greater uncertainty, often in regions with sparse data or high variability.\n")
```

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(kernlab)  # For the spam dataset
library(MASS)     # For LDA and QDA
library(e1071)    # For Naive Bayes
library(pROC)     # For ROC analysis

# Load the spam dataset
data(spam)

# Fit the models
lda_model <- lda(type ~ ., data = spam)  # Linear Discriminant Analysis
qda_model <- qda(type ~ ., data = spam)  # Quadratic Discriminant Analysis
nb_model <- naiveBayes(type ~ ., data = spam)  # Naive Bayes
fld_model <- lda(type ~ ., data = spam)  # Fisher Linear Discriminant (same as LDA)

# Predict probabilities
lda_preds <- predict(lda_model, spam)$posterior[, 2]
qda_preds <- predict(qda_model, spam)$posterior[, 2]
nb_preds <- predict(nb_model, spam, type = "raw")[, 2]
fld_preds <- predict(fld_model, spam)$posterior[, 2]

# Calculate test errors
lda_class <- predict(lda_model, spam)$class
qda_class <- predict(qda_model, spam)$class
nb_class <- predict(nb_model, spam, type = "class")
fld_class <- lda_class  # FLD is equivalent to LDA

lda_error <- mean(lda_class != spam$type)
qda_error <- mean(qda_class != spam$type)
nb_error <- mean(nb_class != spam$type)
fld_error <- lda_error  # Same as LDA

# Print test errors
cat("Test Error Rates:\n")
cat("LDA: ", lda_error, "\n")
cat("QDA: ", qda_error, "\n")
cat("Naive Bayes: ", nb_error, "\n")
cat("FLD: ", fld_error, "\n")

# Generate ROC curves
roc_lda <- roc(spam$type, lda_preds, levels = rev(levels(spam$type)))
roc_qda <- roc(spam$type, qda_preds, levels = rev(levels(spam$type)))
roc_nb <- roc(spam$type, nb_preds, levels = rev(levels(spam$type)))
roc_fld <- roc(spam$type, fld_preds, levels = rev(levels(spam$type)))
# Calculate AUC for each model
auc_lda <- auc(roc_lda)
auc_qda <- auc(roc_qda)
auc_nb <- auc(roc_nb)
auc_fld <- auc(roc_fld)

# Print AUC values
cat("AUC Values:\n")
cat("LDA: ", auc_lda, "\n")
cat("QDA: ", auc_qda, "\n")
cat("Naive Bayes: ", auc_nb, "\n")
cat("FLD: ", auc_fld, "\n")


# Plot ROC curves with fixed x-axis (False Positive Rate)
plot(roc_lda, col = "blue", main = "Comparative ROC Curves", lwd = 2, legacy.axes = TRUE)
lines(roc_qda, col = "red", lwd = 2)
lines(roc_nb, col = "green", lwd = 2)
lines(roc_fld, col = "purple", lwd = 2)

# Add legend
legend("bottomright", legend = c("LDA", "QDA", "Naive Bayes", "FLD"),
       col = c("blue", "red", "green", "purple"), lty = 1, lwd = 2)
citation("pROC")

```
```{r}
library(kernlab)
data(spam)  # Load the spam dataset
library(MASS)
library(e1071)
library(pROC)
library(caret)
# 5. Stratified Holdout and Replications
set.seed(19671210)
S <- 50
test_errors <- data.frame(LDA = numeric(S), QDA = numeric(S), NB = numeric(S), FLD = numeric(S))

for (i in 1:S) {
  index <- createDataPartition(reduced_spam$type, p = 2/3, list = FALSE)
  train_data <- reduced_spam[index, ]
  test_data <- reduced_spam[-index, ]
  
  # Fit models
  lda_model <- lda(type ~ ., data = train_data)
  qda_model <- qda(type ~ ., data = train_data)
  nb_model <- naiveBayes(type ~ ., data = train_data)
  fld_model <- lda(type ~ ., data = train_data)
  
  # Predictions and errors
  lda_pred <- predict(lda_model, test_data)$class
  qda_pred <- predict(qda_model, test_data)$class
  nb_pred <- predict(nb_model, test_data)
  fld_pred <- predict(fld_model, test_data)$class
  
  test_errors[i, ] <- c(
    mean(lda_pred != test_data$type),  # Misclassification rate for LDA
    mean(qda_pred != test_data$type),  # Misclassification rate for QDA
    mean(nb_pred != test_data$type),  # Misclassification rate for Naive Bayes
    mean(fld_pred != test_data$type)  # Misclassification rate for FLD
  )
}
# Print mean test errors for each model
cat("Model Test Errors (mean over", S, "replications):\n")
cat(sprintf("LDA Test Error: %.4f\n", mean(test_errors$LDA)))
cat(sprintf("QDA Test Error: %.4f\n", mean(test_errors$QDA)))
cat(sprintf("Naive Bayes Test Error: %.4f\n", mean(test_errors$NB)))
cat(sprintf("FLD Test Error: %.4f\n", mean(test_errors$FLD)))

# Print mean accuracy for each model
cat("Model Accuracies (mean over", S, "replications):\n")
cat(sprintf("LDA Accuracy: %.2f%%\n", (1 - mean(test_errors$LDA)) * 100))
cat(sprintf("QDA Accuracy: %.2f%%\n", (1 - mean(test_errors$QDA)) * 100))
cat(sprintf("Naive Bayes Accuracy: %.2f%%\n", (1 - mean(test_errors$NB)) * 100))
cat(sprintf("FLD Accuracy: %.2f%%\n", (1 - mean(test_errors$FLD)) * 100))

# 7. Boxplot of test errors
boxplot(test_errors, main = "Comparative Boxplots of Test Errors",
        col = c("blue", "red", "green", "purple"),
        names = c("LDA", "QDA", "Naive Bayes", "FLD"))
```
